surface: deterministic Python reference micro-harness paired to ClayCode candidate semantics
scope_warning: Controlled-German synthetic semantic proxy only. It does not measure general German language coverage, model quality or target-VPS resource cost.
primary_question: Does SPL detect hard-field common-mode translator corruption that ordinary type checks and same-codec roundtrip miss, and does it provide any unique benefit over a strong independent full semantic validator?

corpus.fault_design: Faults are deliberately stable under same-codec normalize/reparse so common-mode roundtrip can appear self-consistent despite wrong source semantics.

baselines: TYPE_ONLY: candidate is a structurally valid typed frame
SAME_CODEC_ROUNDTRIP: buggy source parser -> candidate -> renderer -> same parser and compare candidate stability
CONVENTIONAL_FULL_VALIDATOR: independent full controlled-German semantic parser -> compare complete frame
SPL_SINGLE: narrow per-field partial oracles -> compare candidate hard projection
TWO_FULL_FAULT_CONTAINMENT: one faulty full validator plus one exact full validator
DUAL_SPL_FAULT_CONTAINMENT: one faulty partial-oracle family plus one exact family
controls: per-field sensor ablation on single-field corruption
UNKNOWN hard-field source forms must not ACCEPT
ExpressionState style variants must preserve all hard fields
single checker/oracle fault correlated with translator fault
decision: Defeating weak roundtrip is insufficient. If strong full validator matches SPL correctness and is cheaper, SPL has no unique architecture benefit. If dual SPL only matches two full validators under checker fault injection while costing more in the proxy, fault containment is not unique.
